home.hero_desc: Real-world valuations and buying strategies. Avoid retail traps.
home.voice_appraisal_subtitle: Describe it — I'll give you the dealer's view
home.tip_joints_desc: Machine-cut vs hand-cut tells the era. Irregular is usually a good sign.
home.tip_glass_desc: Real age shows underneath, not on display surfaces.
home.tip_veneer_desc: Check the edges. Thick veneer (1-2mm) usually means pre-1850. Paper-thin is modern.
home.tip_hardware_desc: Look behind the handles. Extra holes suggest the hardware was replaced, affecting value.
home.tip_smell_desc: Old wood has a distinct, musty but not rotten smell. New stains smell like chemicals.

analysis.auction_premium_title: Auction House Fees & Buyer's Premium (Frais de Vente)
analysis.auction_premium_desc: Auction houses charge a mandatory 20%–30% buyer's premium on top of the winning hammer price, plus potential online bidding fees (1.5%–3% on Drouot Digital, Saleroom, LiveAuctioneers). Factor this into your maximum paddle bid.
analysis.share_hard_pass: Dealer Warning: This item is a Hard Pass (Score: {{score}}). {{judgement}}
analysis.share_tier_d: Antique Hunter Alert: This {{title}} is a Tier D utility item. {{judgement}}
analysis.investment_insight_fallback: Only worth buying at a discount — this is not a hold piece. Profit depends entirely on buying below dealer level.
analysis.must_have_insight_fallback: A great purchase for personal enjoyment. The condition is secondary to your aesthetic preference, but do budget for restoration.
analysis.resale_insight_fallback: Profit depends entirely on buying below dealer level. High restoration costs severely limit your margin.
analysis.paddle_rule: Your maximum hammer bid (walk-away) is {{hammer}}. With the {{pct}}% buyer's premium that comes to {{allIn}} all-in. Rule of thumb: maximum hammer bid = your total budget ÷ {{mult}}.
analysis.reason_strong_buy: {{price}}{{premium}} is at or below the market low ({{low}}) – clear room for a dealer margin.
analysis.reason_good_buy: {{price}}{{premium}} is in the lower half of the market range ({{low}}–{{high}}) – a good buy if condition holds.
analysis.reason_fair: {{price}}{{premium}} is in the upper half of the market range ({{low}}–{{high}}) – fair, but little margin left.
analysis.reason_overpriced: {{price}}{{premium}} is above the market high ({{high}}) – you would be paying retail-level money.
analysis.reason_walk_away: {{price}}{{premium}} is above the top of the retail range ({{retailHigh}}) – no margin at this price.
analysis.reason_high_risk: The photos show a serious authenticity or condition risk, so the price alone does not make this a buy.
analysis.reason_no_price: Add the asking price or estimate to get a buy verdict.
analysis.reason_above_walk_away: {{price}}{{premium}} is above your walk-away price ({{walkAway}}) – overpriced, no margin left. Don't go above {{walkAway}}.
analysis.reason_above_smart_buy: {{price}}{{premium}} is above the smart-buy price ({{smartBuy}}) but within your walk-away ({{walkAway}}) – fair, but little margin left.
analysis.reason_need_evidence: We can't confirm the period yet, so no buy verdict at {{price}}{{premium}}. The provisional range is {{low}} – {{high}}; add the evidence below and re-run.
analysis.dealer_scale_note: Shop, dealer and private asking prices are judged against the dealer range. The auction range is what the piece would make at auction (hammer, before fees).
analysis.reason_dealer_strong_buy: {{price}} is at or below the auction mid ({{auctionMid}}) – a strong buy for a shop price.
analysis.reason_dealer_good_buy: {{price}} is at or below {{goodTop}} (the lower of the auction high and the dealer low) – a good shop price.
analysis.reason_dealer_fair: {{price}} is within the dealer range ({{dealerLow}}–{{dealerHigh}}) – a fair shop price.
analysis.reason_dealer_overpriced: {{price}} is above the dealer high ({{dealerHigh}}) – overpriced, even for a shop. Don't go above {{dealerHigh}}.
analysis.reason_dealer_walk_away: {{price}} is well above the dealer range (over {{overTop}}) – walk away.

checklist.title: Before you buy
checklist.intro: Check each point on the piece itself, then tap Yes, No or Not sure. Re-running with your answers firms up the range and confidence (confirmations) or lowers them (denials).

where.seat_rail: on the seat rail (under the seat, front or back rail)
where.carcass: on the carcass (top of the uprights, back or inside)

items.stamp_every_piece: The {{maker}} stamp is present and legible on each of the {{n}} pieces, {{where}}.
items.stamp_present: The {{maker}} stamp is present and legible {{where}}.
items.label_is_not_stamp: Beyond the dealer's label: is there a real {{maker}} stamp on the piece itself? A label proves nothing.
items.matching_set: The {{n}} pieces match: same wood, carving, dimensions and construction (not a married or completed set).
items.joints_underneath: Underneath: pegged joints, hand-cut joints and hand-saw marks, old oxidised wood — no machine cuts, screws or staples.
items.seat_rails_webbing: Seat frame and rails are original under the fabric (no new rails, sound webbing).
items.mirror_glass_original: The glass is original (old mercury or early silvering, slight waves and foxing — not modern float glass).
items.mirror_back_original: The back is original: old wooden planks, hand-made nails, consistent oxidation.
items.crest_original: The crest (fronton) is original to the frame: same wood, carving and gilding, old fixings.
items.gilding_original: Gilding is old (water gilding, wear on the high points), not a recent re-gild or gold paint.
items.marble_original: The marble top is original to the piece (fits exactly, old underside, no modern cut).
items.hardware_original: Handles, mounts and escutcheons are original (old fixings, matching holes, no extra holes).
items.veneer_sound: Veneer and marquetry are sound (no large losses, lifting or modern patches).
items.no_major_restoration: No major restoration: replaced legs or rails, new elements, heavy refinishing.
items.invoice_wording: The invoice will say {{wording}}, with a description of the piece and any restorations.
items.provenance_condition_report: Ask the seller for provenance and a written condition report (restorations, replacements).

comps.title: Maker & auction comparables

status_note.stamped_confirmed: Valued as a stamped piece by this maker.
status_note.stamped_stated: Valued as a stamped piece, as stated — check it yourself.
status_note.stamp_in_photo: A stamp is visible in your photos — confirm it is legible on every piece.
status_note.attributed: An attribution, not a stamp: valued between an unattributed piece and a stamped one.
status_note.dealer_label: A dealer's label is not a stamp: valued as an unattributed piece of the period.
status_note.doubtful_stamp: Stamp looks transplanted, fake or inconsistent with the construction: no maker premium.
status_note.mentioned: No stamp confirmed: valued as an unattributed piece of the period.

comps.jme_note: JME / jurande mark mentioned — supporting guild evidence when genuine, never a maker by itself.
comps.stamp_warning: Check the {{maker}} stamp on EVERY piece yourself, and have it written on the invoice (« estampillé {{maker}} »). Without it, the maker premium does not apply.
comps.anchored_all_in: Range anchored on {{n}} verified auction results: median {{median}} per piece incl. fees, × {{pieces}}.
comps.anchored_hammer: Range anchored on {{n}} verified auction results: median {{median}} per piece (hammer), × {{pieces}}.

fallback.too_few: Too few verified results of the same kind to anchor the range — the range is the appraiser's estimate.
fallback.not_stamped: Shown for reference only: without a stamp or attribution, these results do not set the range.
fallback.none_verified: No verified auction results found for {{maker}} — the range is the appraiser's estimate.
fallback.error: The auction results search failed — the range is the appraiser's estimate.

comps.verified_note: Each result was opened and checked on the auction house's own page (maker, piece and sold price). Nothing unverified is shown.

negotiate.title: Negotiate
negotiate.suggestion_note: Suggestions from this appraisal, not a guarantee of what the seller will accept.
negotiate.walk_note: Never go above your walk-away of {{walk}}.
negotiate.asking_over: The asking price is {{pct}}% above that walk-away: be ready to walk.
negotiate.pay_cash: Offer cash for a quick sale: dealers often take {{lo}}–{{hi}}% off{{amount}}. In France, a French tax resident may pay a professional in cash up to {{cap}} (art. D112-3 CMF); ask for an invoice.
negotiate.pay_cash_private: Cash usually helps with a private seller ({{lo}}–{{hi}}% off is typical{{amount}}). Get a signed receipt with the description, date and price.
negotiate.pay_private_trader: If the seller is in fact a trader (brocanteur, market professional), French law caps cash at {{cap}}: pay by transfer instead.
negotiate.pay_transfer: No cash here: in France, cash payments to a professional are capped at {{cap}} for French tax residents ({{capNr}} for non-residents buying privately, art. D112-3 CMF). Offer instead to pay today by instant transfer or card and take it away now: a sure, immediate sale is your lever.

levers.bundle: Buying several pieces? Ask for a price for the lot.
levers.delivery: Ask for delivery (or packing) to be included in the price.
levers.timing: End of the day, the end of a fair or the end of the season are good moments to negotiate.
